questions.q: What does a Cosmos DB IP firewall rule actually do?
options: Restricts the public endpoint to an allow-list of specific IP addresses or CIDR ranges, while the public endpoint itself still exists
Removes the account's public endpoint entirely
Encrypts all traffic between the client and Cosmos DB
Grants read-only access to any IP not explicitly blocked
questions.explain: A firewall rule filters who can reach the still-existing public endpoint — it doesn't remove that public surface.

questions.q: What is a Private Endpoint for Cosmos DB?
options: A private-IP network interface provisioned inside your VNet, using Azure Private Link, that maps directly to your Cosmos DB account
A second public IP address reserved exclusively for your account
A firewall rule that only allows traffic from Azure services
A feature that encrypts account keys at rest
questions.explain: A Private Endpoint gives the account a private IP inside your own VNet via Azure Private Link.

questions.q: What is the key structural difference between a firewall rule and a Private Endpoint, per this lesson?
options: A firewall rule filters access to a public endpoint that still exists; a Private Endpoint can remove the public endpoint from the picture entirely
They are functionally identical mechanisms with different names
A firewall rule works only for RBAC-based access, and Private Endpoints only for key-based access
A Private Endpoint is slower but otherwise equivalent to a firewall rule
questions.explain: This is the core distinction the lesson draws: filtering a public surface versus removing it by disabling public network access.

questions.q: How does DNS resolution work once a Private Endpoint is configured for Cosmos DB?
options: A private DNS zone redirects the account's normal hostname to the private IP, so application connection strings don't need to change
Applications must hardcode the private IP address directly, since DNS no longer works
DNS resolution is disabled entirely once a Private Endpoint is created
The account gets an entirely new hostname that must be updated in every application
questions.explain: A private DNS zone transparently redirects the existing hostname to the private IP.

questions.q: When does this lesson suggest IP firewall rules are a reasonable choice over a Private Endpoint?
options: For scenarios with a small number of known, stable public IPs, like dev/test environments or a single office
Firewall rules should never be used under any circumstances
Only for production workloads handling sensitive data
Firewall rules and Private Endpoints cannot be used during the same migration
questions.explain: Firewall rules are quick to set up and reasonable for simple, stable-IP scenarios, while Private Endpoints are recommended for production.
